 ‘GTA 6’ is introducing a new kind of mission: being a good partner 
 A video game that has often been the center of controversy over its content is challenging the franchise’s hypermasculine traditions around gender and relationships.
 The “GTA” series has a reputation for hypermasculine destruction, violence and debauchery. But love, relationships, joy and heartache are also themes in the new 70-hour installment. 
 (Rockstar Games) 
 Mariel Padilla 
 General Assignment Reporter
 Published
 2026-11-20 09:21 
 9:21 
 November 20, 2026 
 am 
 America/Chicago

 “ Grand Theft Auto VI,” also referred to as “GTA 6,” is the latest in the crime-spree, action-packed series from Rockstar Games. It’s the first new installment since 2013 and was one of the most anticipated video games of the year.
 The game is a cultural phenomenon: Even before Thursday’s launch, the game had made more than a billion dollars in presales, with more than 11 million copies, according to SensorTower, a research firm that tracks sales data. 
 Players were encouraged to download and install the game files onto their consoles before its official launch so they could play right when it unlocked. This preloading of the game proved an early test for broadband networks and pushed traffic to record levels. Comcast reported that “GTA 6” pre-loads were the largest single event in its network history, and Spectrum said gaming download traffic on its network rose up to 50 percent.

 What’s different this time 
 This is the first time in “GTA” history that a woman protagonist isn’t optional. Her name is Lucia Caminos, a Latina who just got out of prison. (Rockstar Games) 
 This is the first time in “GTA” history that a woman protagonist isn’t optional. Her name is Lucia Caminos, and she’s a Latina who just got out of prison. In the game’s storyline, she teams up with another character, Jason Duval, in a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style criminal and romantic partnership. 
 The “GTA” series has a reputation for hypermasculine destruction, violence and debauchery. But love, relationships, joy and heartache are also themes in the new 70-hour installment. 
 In addition to robbing stores, crashing cars and shooting pedestrians, players can also put up drywall around the house, buy flowers, shop together, respond to texts promptly, and remember to say goodnight if Jason and Lucia are not together. Romantic closeness is a metric tracked in the game and shapes the story, dialogue and endings
 The game also includes a nonbinary character: Cygnus, a museum curator. The actor Jesse James Rose wrote about their recording experience in an Instagram post and noted that the studio was mindful of their safety not only on set, but also in the game: “To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character,” Rose wrote.
 Past controversy 
 The franchise has long faced criticism that its characters are misogynistic, rely on racial stereotypes, exhibit extreme violence and partake in sexually explicit activities. 
 Critics have condemned the way women were portrayed primarily as strippers, prostitutes or nagging relatives — and rarely as an autonomous main character. Players used to have the ability to solicit, assault and murder sex workers to reclaim spent money in the game. 
 In 2014, some retailers removed “GTA V” from their shelves following a petition accusing the game of glamorizing sexual violence against women. 
 Critics have also argued that the series relies heavily on broad racial stereotypes — particularly in its portrayals of Black, Hispanic and Asian characters — for its criminal gangs and comedic relief.

 The masculinity midterms
 The initial reaction from women gamers 
 Women gamers are largely praising the game, highlighting how it includes representation and relationships, shifting away from the hypermasculine tone. 
 Dr. Esther Lapite-Garrett, a psychologist and gamer, told Yahoo Tech that she’s excited to see Lucia bring Latina representation to the game.  
 “Maybe some of those hypermasculine and sexualized characteristics in previous games are going to continue to exist in this game, and technically, you can do some of those things too as a woman,” Lapite-Garrett said. “But the potential of being able to have a woman be part of this huge game series in a way that’s maybe not super centered on this hypermasculine, sexualized, erotic focus, and instead having actual gameplay moments that have nuance and meaning, I think is so exciting.”
 Krysttl, a gamer who has tens of thousands of followers and subscribers on Twitch, YouTube and Instagram, said she was initially hesitant about “GTA 6” because she was worried the game would lean too heavily into romance. 
 But after watching the launch trailer, she changed her mind and said in a reaction video that she was “excited to see what the missions are.” After playing the game, she called it , “one of the most impressive games ever.” 
 Of course, not everyone is happy 
 Some men are angry that they have to be nice and respect their girlfriend as part of the gameplay. (Rockstar Games) 
 In response to “GTA 6” footage released in August, YouTuber AndyPants Gaming — a right-leaning account with more than 340,000 followers — accused the game of being “feminist slop.” The sentiment was echoed by other influencers and fans online. 
 Some men are angry that they have to be nice and respect their girlfriend as part of the gameplay. 
 Steven Crowder, a conservative commentator with millions of followers, posted his ire on social media on launch day. He listed things players can’t do anymore in GTA 6, including kissing anyone but “your strong Latina female partner,” shooting gay bars, picking up hookers and killing protesters.
 “Listen, hookers and killing are bad, I agree,” he wrote. “But this isn’t about the Left suddenly becoming moral, it’s just selectively enforcing their twisted version of morality.”

 Crowder got divorced in 2021, which he has said was not his choice . A home surveillance video later emerged of him berating his pregnant wife about not doing her “wifely things.” 
 “GTA is insanely cucked, half of the missions are jestermaxing and simping for girls,” Braden Peters, also known as Clavicular, the “looksmaxxing” streamer with millions of followers, posted on social media. Peters was indicted on two rape counts; he has pleaded not guilty to the charges. 
 The relational aspect of this new installment has also provoked an unexpectedly vehement response from others who argue that playing the game could amount to cheating on your real-life partner. 
 In a TikTok video viewed more than 600,000 times, Shelby Haas said: “In absolutely no human way is my fiancé playing ‘GTA VI.’ You literally have to maintain a relationship with a girl. You have to take her on dates, and you can have sex with her. Don’t let your boyfriend or fiancé or husband play ‘GTA 6.’”
